messages:
jamie.ops: alert: multiple control-plane heartbeats missing from sjc2. monitoring shows API errors + node count drop. first saw this at ~2265004300.
oncall-bot: incident created: sjc2-region-degradation (severity: P1). paging: @raj.sre @maria-infra
raj.sre: copying checks: provider console, BGP, control plane pods, kube-apiserver logs. anyone nearby to run quick network traceroute? :eyes:
maria-infra: running quick cluster checks: `kubectl get nodes -o wide --context=sjc2` -> 12 nodes NotReady, several reporting kubelet crashloop. past 5m CPU ops on control-plane nodes spiked.
kevin-plateng: seeing identical in infra telemetry: all gpus in sjc2 show disconnected in fleet-manager. metrics show sudden drop in capacity from 480 -> 28 GPUs.
luis-net: I kicked off cloud provider health API check, BGP sessions to our peering look flapping. Provider status page shows "network disruption affecting SJC region".
sophie-eng: any ongoing deploys? deploy-bot: `deploy started` earlier? @deploy-bot can you confirm recent deploys to sjc2?
deploy-bot: last deploy to sjc2 was 2265004200, rollout completed. No immediate rollback by deploy-bot.
raj.sre: ok, treat as region-level network/hosting failure. Start the failover runbook: 1) stop scheduling to sjc2, 2) warm up fallback capacity in sfo1, iad2, 3) shift DNS/loadbalancer routing.
maria-infra: setting cluster-autoscaler scale-down off for affected clusters; creating additional node pools in sfo1 with accelerated GPUs. Kickoff: `terraform apply` to provision 60 g4x nodes (on-demand) as a temporary.
kevin-plateng: note: on-demand GPUs will blow our burn rate — will show in cost dashboard. but we need capacity to keep SLAs.
jamie.ops: initiated traffic-shift: set LB weight sjc2 -> 0 over 30s window, ramping others. lowering TTL for edge DNS to 30s.
luis-net: started DNS failover in provider console, routing to sfo1 and iad2 via global balancer. also enforced: avoid cross-region egress loops.
sophie-eng: starting canary reroutes for critical hosts only (api endpoints), leaving low-priority tasks queued (batch jobs paused).
raj.sre: assigning incident roles: IC=raj.sre, comms=jamie.ops, infra=maria-infra, network=luis-net. escalation to on-call SRE manager if no recovery in 15m.
maria-infra: pasted quick logs from control plane nodes:
```
Mar  3 12:10:02 kubelet[1234]: E0323 12:10:02.123 kubelet.go:213] failed to register node: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
Mar  3 12:11:10 containerd[1]: grpc: the connection is unavailable
```
kevin-plateng: provider confirms packet loss across their fabric in sjc region, likely MTT issue. no ETA yet. recommend we keep failover active and avoid manual reboots of fleet nodes.
jamie.ops: comms: drafting status update for customers: "We detected a regional networking disruption impacting SJC2. Traffic is being shifted to other regions; some requests may see higher latency. We're provisioning extra GPU capacity; working on restoring normal operations. Next update in 10 minutes." @kevin-plateng please review.
kevin-plateng: LGTM. add note about potential increased costs and temporary limits on heavy batch jobs.
raj.sre: immediate mitigation = traffic shift + provision in fallback regions. long term: postmortem to cover provider resilience options and cross-region warm pool sizes.
maria-infra: autoscaling events started in sfo1; provisioning reports 40/60 new nodes booted, nvidia drivers installing.
sophie-eng: we've paused non-critical background jobs to preserve new capacity for latency-sensitive endpoints.
jamie.ops: folks, if you see >5% error rate on any route after cutover, mark as degradation. next sync in 10m. IC out.
oncall-bot: next scheduled update reminder in 10 minutes.
